references.text: The same chapter describes how the Israelites did not listen to the judges, but committed spiritual adultery with other gods and bowed down to them.
The Israelites did what was evil in the Lord's sight and forgot the Lord their God, serving the Baals and the Asherah poles.
The Israelites again did what was evil in the Lord's sight, a recurring pattern of apostasy.
After Ehud died, the Israelites again did what was evil in the Lord's sight.
The Israelites continued to do evil and served the Baals, the Ashtoreths, and other foreign gods.
Moses describes the people of Israel as a stiff-necked people who will not let go of their evil ways.
Moses asks the Lord to look past the people's stubbornness and wickedness, which reflect their hard path.
Solomon turned to other gods in his old age and did what was evil in the Lord's sight.
Jeremiah describes how Israel's fathers would not listen and were stiff-necked, and each generation became worse than the one before.
Ezekiel warns the people against following their fathers' example and committing spiritual adultery with their idols.
Hosea compares Israel to a stubborn heifer that will not be led.
